advice: Practice timed 90-minute, 4-level simulators (in-memory KV DB with TTL and scans, bank with transaction log, task manager with dependencies) in Python with only the standard library. Minimize bugs, since every test at a level must pass to move on.

Master the web crawler end to end: BFS restricted to the same host, then thread-pool or async workers with a thread-safe visited set and clean termination. Don't announce that you've memorized it; that has led to an extra round and a downlevel.

For any cache or store problem, expect follow-ups on thread safety, error handling and persistence or crash recovery (e.g. a write-ahead log). Keep the code running at each step rather than over-engineering serialization.

Prepare a real 'Why Anthropic', read the culture documents the recruiter sends, and be ready to give an honest critique of Anthropic's direction and to reason through ethical dilemmas several follow-ups deep.
For system design, treat LLM prompts as classic infra: batching up to the GPU limit, queues, routing, backpressure and overload, observability. Narrate trade-offs collaboratively.
interview_format: Anthropic runs one generalist SWE loop. Public reports are rarely labeled mid-level, so level-specific details are low confidence. The usual sequence is a recruiter screen, then a 90-minute CodeSignal 'Industry Coding Assessment' (one stateful system built up over 4 levels, usually in Python), sometimes followed by a ~60-minute live practical coding screen, then a hiring manager screen. The virtual onsite on Google Meet has 4–5 rounds of about 55 minutes: practical coding, system design (often infra/inference flavored), project deep dive, a culture/values round with deep ethical follow-ups, and a hiring manager behavioral round. Coding is practical rather than classic LeetCode and checks fast, correct, extensible code, concurrency and persistence; team matching happens after the onsite.

web_report:
# How Anthropic interviews mid-level (2–5 yrs) software engineers — research report

**Before you rely on this:**
- **Almost nothing here is specific to mid-level.** Public reports are usually just labeled "Software Engineer." The labeled ones are mostly Senior or Staff, and I've marked those. Treat level-specific statements as low confidence.
- **I hit the search tool's limit after about 10 queries.** That stopped me from searching Reddit (r/leetcode, r/cscareerquestions) and LeetCode Discuss directly, and none of those threads showed up in the searches I did run.
- **Where the evidence comes from.** First-hand sources are Glassdoor, Blind, PracHub write-ups and one Exponent write-up. Prep companies (IGotAnOffer, Aced/Exponent, HelloInterview, DesignGurus, InterviewQuery, TrueInterview) summarize candidate reports, so they count as second-hand. Dates are relative to page timestamps, which run up to about Sept 2026.

---

## 1. The interview loop

The order varies somewhat between reports. This is the most common sequence.

| # | Stage | Length / platform | What it assesses | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Resume screen / application | — | — | https://igotanoffer.com/en/advice/anthropic-software-engineer-interview |
| 1 | **Recruiter screen**, sometimes split into two calls | 15–30 min | Why Anthropic, background, AI safety views, level, logistics. A Glassdoor Senior candidate (NY) said "why do you want to join" was a main question. interviewing.io says strong candidates fail here because they "haven't done the reading." | https://trueinterview.io/study/anthropic-software-engineer-interview-process ; https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/Anthropic-Senior-Software-Engineer-Interview-Questions-EI_IE8109027.0,9_KO10,34.htm ; https://interviewing.io/anthropic-interview-questions |
| 2 | **CodeSignal online assessment** (CodeSignal calls this format the "Industry Coding Assessment"). Some candidates get a live technical screen instead. | 90 min, one stateful system built up over 4 levels, usually in Python with the standard library. You must pass every test at one level to unlock the next. Some report a six-part version. The live alternative is 60–90 min in Google Colab with an interviewer. | Writing practical code fast, reading specs carefully, extensibility | https://www.hellointerview.com/guides/anthropic/swe ; https://interviewing.io/anthropic-interview-questions ; https://trueinterview.io/study/anthropic-software-engineer-interview-process ; https://www.aced.io/guides/anthropic-software-engineer-interview |
| 3 | **Technical phone screen** (live coding). Reported in addition to the OA in some loops. | ~60 min | Practical coding with follow-ups. Examples: LRU cache, web crawler. | https://prachub.com/interview-experiences/anthropic-software-engineer-interview-experience-oa-a-python-lru-cache-phone-screen-and-rejection-after-a-full-onsite |
| 4 | **Hiring manager screen** | 45–60 min. May include code review. | Architectural reasoning (what fails first under load, observability), judgment, team fit | https://igotanoffer.com/en/advice/anthropic-interview-questions ; https://www.designgurus.io/blog/anthropic-interview-process |
| 5 | **Virtual onsite**, Google Meet | 4–5 rounds of ~55 min. Some say it's split over two days with 7–9 rounds in total. | See the onsite rounds below. | https://igotanoffer.com/en/advice/anthropic-software-engineer-interview ; https://www.designgurus.io/blog/anthropic-interview-process |
| 6 | References + team matching | 2–4 weeks | Team matching happens after the onsite, not before. | https://interviewing.io/anthropic-interview-questions |

**Onsite rounds.** One generic SWE candidate (Mar 2026) listed every round: coding (web crawler), system design (batching GPU requests), project deep dive, a culture round with "nonstop follow-up questions," and a hiring manager round (most impactful project plus standard behavioral questions). https://prachub.com/interview-experiences/anthropic-software-engineer-interview-experience-oa-a-python-lru-cache-phone-screen-and-rejection-after-a-full-onsite

- **Coding:** practical problems rather than LeetCode. https://www.aced.io/blog/anthropic-interview-process
- **System design:** see section 4.
- **Project deep dive:** walk through a past project in detail.
- **Culture / values:**
  - Two interviewers, one asking and one shadowing. They probe ethics and moral conflicts 3–4 follow-ups deep. Aced calls it the round with the highest failure rate. https://www.aced.io/blog/anthropic-interview-process
  - A Senior/L5 Safeguards candidate said non-technical staff ran it and it felt "almost like a therapy session." https://www.tryexponent.com/experiences/anthropic-senior-software-engineer-interview-2ffa5f
- **Hiring manager:** behavioral questions and impact.

**Coding-round rules.** One Glassdoor Senior reviewer said you could use your local environment and the internet, but no AI assistants. The same page says Anthropic gives no feedback as a policy. https://www.glassdoor.ca/Interview/Anthropic-Senior-Software-Engineer-Interview-Questions-EI_IE8109027.0,9_KO10,34.htm

**How the loop differs by level and team:**
- **Staff+:** Blind commenters (~3 weeks ago) disagree on whether coding was dropped. Some had no coding round; others had coding as recently as two weeks earlier. https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-no-coding-interview-anymore-wm66qjrz
- **Staff, downleveled:** one Staff candidate admitted they'd seen the crawler question before, got an extra coding round, and was downleveled to Senior. https://prachub.com/interview-experiences/anthropic-staff-software-engineer-interview-experience-a-surprise-extra-round-then-a-downlevel-to-senior
- **Team flavor:** TrueInterview says there is one SWE loop, with problems tilted toward the hiring team (inference designs for infra teams, product designs for full-stack). https://trueinterview.io/study/anthropic-software-engineer-interview-process
- **Infra roles:** one infra-oriented candidate's onsite included distributed coding and hardware reasoning. https://prachub.com/interview-experiences/anthropic-software-engineer-interview-experience-distributed-coding-ai-safety-and-hardware-reasoning
- **Mid-level specifically:** no source found.

Staff variant: fix a given implementation, then make it persistent. ## 3. Practical / non-LeetCode coding rounds

Practical coding is the norm at Anthropic.

- **CodeSignal OA:** one system that grows over 4 levels. A Senior reviewer said level 1 was trivial and level 2 was "like a leetcode hard," which you must pass to reach levels 3–4. https://www.glassdoor.ca/Interview/Anthropic-Senior-Software-Engineer-Interview-Questions-EI_IE8109027.0,9_KO10,34.htm
  - A Glassdoor (London) reviewer said the tests come in a read-only file. https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/Anthropic-Senior-Software-Engineer-Interview-Questions-EI_IE8109027.0,9_KO10,34.htm
  - The main constraint is time; you need to keep mistakes to a minimum. https://www.glassdoor.co.uk/Interview/Anthropic-Interview-Questions-E8109027.htm
- **Concurrency:** the web crawler moves from single-threaded to multi-worker. https://gist.github.com/nito-Q/3b0e09676de3b1176f85e2db3d09a9ad
- **Persistence / durability:** the follow-up to the LRU cache is crash recovery and serialization. https://prachub.com/interview-experiences/anthropic-software-engineer-interview-experience-oa-a-python-lru-cache-phone-screen-and-rejection-after-a-full-onsite

## 5. Topic emphasis

1. **Stateful system design in code:** hash maps, TTL, ordered scans. This is the OA's core.
2. **Caching:** LRU, hashable keys, persistence.
3. **Graph traversal (BFS/DFS) plus concurrency:** threads, async, worker pools.
4. **Stacks and event processing:** the profiler problem.
5. **Distributed aggregation:** for infra teams.

Classic LeetCode grinding comes up less. One Blind commenter summed it up as "OpenAI leetcode, anthropic not leetcode," though others still found it hard. https://www.teamblind.com/post/do-openai-and-anthropic-still-expect-you-to-manually-leetcode-mbzzci4i

## 6. Advice that recurs across reports

- **Prepare a real "Why Anthropic" and a position on its values.**
  - The recruiter sends culture documents, and the culture round opens with your reading of them. https://www.aced.io/guides/anthropic-software-engineer-interview
  - Expect to be asked for an honest critique of Anthropic's direction. https://www.aced.io/blog/anthropic-interview-process
  - One Blind commenter said the questions resemble Amazon's Leadership Principles questions (low confidence). https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-culture-interview-syng3rar
- **Expect layered follow-ups.** Narrate your thinking and treat the round as collaboration. https://igotanoffer.com/en/advice/anthropic-software-engineer-interview
- **Practice 90-minute, 4-level simulators against the clock:** bank, database, task manager. https://trueinterview.io/study/anthropic-software-engineer-interview-process
- **Keep code running.** One candidate spent so long on serialization that their code never ran. https://prachub.com/interview-experiences/anthropic-staff-software-engineer-interview-experience-a-surprise-extra-round-then-a-downlevel-to-senior
- **Memorized answers can backfire.** Interviewers may watch for over-rehearsed solutions https://interviewing.io/anthropic-interview-questions, and the Staff candidate who said they'd seen the crawler before got an extra round.
- **You don't need ML experience for SWE roles.** https://interviewing.io/anthropic-interview-questions
- **Expect a hard, sometimes fast process.**
  - Blind posters called it "the HARDEST" loop they'd done, and one finished in 8 working days. https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-megathread-6estt896
  - Glassdoor rates difficulty 3.6/5, with a 30% positive experience rate. https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/Anthropic-Software-Engineer-Interview-Questions-EI_IE8109027.0,9_KO10,27.htm
